ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a straight race track from Start on the left to Finish on the right. The positions of water stations are marked below the track, and Water 1, Water 2, ..., Water 7 can be seen, indicating that there are 7 water stations evenly distributed between the starting point and the finishing point. Reasoning: Let the total course length be L miles. The 7 evenly distributed water stations divide the distance from the starting point to the finishing point into 8 equal intervals, so the 3rd water station is 3L/8 from the starting point. The problem also says that there are 2 repair stations evenly distributed between the starting point and the finishing point, so they divide the whole course into 3 equal intervals, and the 1st repair station is L/3 from the starting point. It is known that the 3rd water station is 2 miles after the 1st repair station, therefore 3L/8 - L/3 = 2. Getting a common denominator gives 9L/24 - 8L/24 = 2, that is, L/24 = 2, so L = 48.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a straight race route from Start to Finish with 7 interior water-station positions labeled Water 1, Water 2, ..., Water 7, equally spaced along the route. From the text, note that 2 repair stations are also equally spaced between Start and Finish, and that Water 3 is 2 miles after Repair 1. Let the race length be L. Seven equally spaced water stations create 8 equal gaps, so Water 3 is at 3L/8 from the start. Two equally spaced repair stations create 3 equal gaps, so Repair 1 is at L/3 from the start. Use the given bridge that Water 3 is 2 miles after Repair 1: 3L/8 - L/3 = 2. Solve L/24 = 2, so L = 48 miles.

method.method_draft: Read the picture as a single straight race course with Start at the left, Finish at the right, and 7 evenly spaced water stations in order along the route. From the text, add the unseen 2 evenly spaced repair stations. Instead of using variables first, overlay a common subdivision of the race: water stations divide the race into 8 equal water-intervals, while repair stations divide it into 3 equal repair-intervals. The least common multiple of 8 and 3 is 24, so imagine the whole route divided into 24 equal small segments. Water 3 is after 3 water-intervals, i.e. 3 × 3 = 9 small segments from the start. Repair 1 is after 1 repair-interval, i.e. 8 small segments from the start. Their separation is 1 small segment, and the text says that separation is 2 miles. Therefore all 24 small segments total 24 × 2 = 48 miles.
